overview: 오늘 스냅샷은 중순의 동반 매수 파동이 거의 모든 자산군에서 홀드로 되돌려지며 방향성 공백 상태에 진입했음을 보여준다. 주식·암호화폐 등 위험자산군이 8월 13~21일의 매수 신호를 일제히 청산하고 홀드로 수렴한 반면, 안전자산군 내에서는 채권(TLT·IEF)이 장기 매도 추세를 멈추고 홀드로 안착한 반면 달러(UUP)만 지속적인 매도 편향을 유지해 자산군 간 위험 선호·회피 신호가 명확히 갈리지 않는 혼재 양상을 띤다. 인플레이션 헤지군도 금·광범위 원자재·에너지·천연가스·비철금속이 모두 홀드로 정렬된 가운데 농산물(DBA)만 홀로 매수를 지속하며 섹터 내 괴리를 키우고 있는데, 이는 거시적 리플레이션 베팅이라기보다 개별 수급 요인에 기댄 선별적 강세로 읽힌다. 종합하면 시장은 최근 며칠 사이 위험자산과 헤지자산이 동시에 매수로 전환했다가 다시 동시에 홀드로 후퇴하는 '허수 진동'을 거친 뒤, 달러 약세라는 단일 구조적 흐름만을 남긴 채 다음 촉매를 기다리는 대기 국면에 들어선 것으로 보인다.

추천: 매수

**근거:**

**1. 기계적 매매 신호 (최우선 판단 기준)**
- **진입 조건 충족:** 종가(28.82)가 20일 돈치안 채널 상단을 상향 돌파(`20일 상단 돌파 여부: True`)하며 명확한 **매수 진입 신호**를 발생시켰습니다.
- **청산 조건 미충족:** 트레일링 스탑(28.07) 대비 종가가 0.75포인트 이상 여유 있게 위에 있어(`청산 시그널: False`), 현재 추세를 위협하는 매도 신호는 없습니다.
- **거래량 확인:** `거래량 급증: True`로, 돌파 시점에 시장 참여자들의 적극적인 매수세가 동반되었음을 확인했습니다. 이는 허위 돌파 가능성을 낮춰주는 확인 신호입니다.

**2. 뉴스 팩트의 추세 뒷받침 여부 (DBA 펀더멘털 직결)**
DBA(Invesco DB Agriculture Fund)는 옥수수, 대두, 밀, 설탕, 커피, 카카오, 면화 등 주요 농산물 선물 바스켓을 추종하므로, 곡물 섹터의 수급 악화와 강세장 진입 소식은 **펀더멘털상 상승 추세의 '연료'가 되는 하드 팩트**입니다.

- **ADM Investor Services / Pro Farmer 리포트 (가장 직접적 증거):**  
  기사는 **"옥수수 9월물이 2년 반 만에 $5 상회, 12월물 신고가 경신"**했으며, **"미국 작물 등급이 57% G/E로 하락(예상 하회)하고 프로파머 투어 수확량 전망치가 USDA 대비 낮게 나옴"**으로써 공급 측 타이트함을 확인시켜 줍니다. 더불어 **"비상업적(펀드) 순매수 포지션이 32만 계약으로 3개월 최대"**라며, 추세를 주도하는 큰손 자금이 이미 강세 베팅에 올라탔음을 보여줍니다. 밀 역시 **"일일 가격제한폭까지 급등하며 신고가"**를 기록했습니다. 이는 DBA 편입 비중이 높은 옥수수·밀·대두가 동시에 **구조적 강세장(New Bull Leg)에 진입했음**을 입증하며, 금일 20일선 돌파가 단순한 기술적 반등이 아님을 뒷받침합니다.

- **Citi "Super El Niño" 리스크 분석 (중장기 추세 지속성 근거):**  
  씨티는 **"NOAA 기준 90% 이상 확률로 1950년 이후 최강급 슈퍼 엘니뇨 발생 예상(10~12월)"**이라며, 이를 옥수수·대두·밀 3개월·12개월 목표가를 일괄 상향(`옥수수 $5.40→$5.90, 대두 $12.75→$13.25, 밀 $7.25→$7.75`)하는 근거로 제시했습니다. **"생산 리스크 프레임워크상 가격이 하방 리스크를 과소평가 중"**이라는 진단은, 현재 돌파가 시작된 추세가 기상 이변이라는 **구조적 드라이버를 등에 업고 상당 기간 지속될 수 있음을 시사**합니다.

**3. 일목균형표 보조 지표 (리스크 관리 관점)**
- **구름 위 · 양운(상승 구름):** 기계적 매수 신호와 **완전히 부합하는 강세 구조**입니다. 현재 가격이 구름 위에 안착해 있고 선행스팬도 상승 전환 중이므로, 진입 후 즉각적인 되돌림 리스크는 낮습니다. 별도의 비중 축소 없이 **표준 포지션 사이즈로 진입**하면 됩니다.

**결론:** 20일 채널 상향 돌파라는 **기계적 진입 규칙**이 발동했고, **거래량 급증**으로 확인되었으며, **곡물 바스켓 전체를 관통하는 공급 차질(작물 등급 하락, 엘니뇨, 흑해 물류 차질)과 펀드 롱 포지션 확대**라는 펀더멘털 팩트가 추세 지속을 강력히 지지합니다. 보조 지표인 일목 구름도 강세 정배열입니다. 이에 **즉시 매수 진입**을 권고합니다. 손절 라인은 기계적 규칙대로 트레일링 스탑(현재 28.07)을 준수하며 추세를 탑니다.

news.title: Ag Market View for Aug 26.2026 - ADM Investor Services
news.summary:
Ag Market View for Aug 26, 2026 (ADM Investor Services) - Key takeaways for agricultural commodities:

Corn
- Prices up ~0.08–0.10, closing near session highs; Sept-26 above $5 for first time in ~2.5 years.
- Dec-26 hits new contract highs late in the session.
- Crop ratings drop to 57% good/excellent (lower than expected); average US yield forecast around 180.1 bpa with production ~15.953 bb, about 60 mbu below USDA forecast.
- Fund positioning: non-commercials' net long ~321k contracts (likely >330k post-session), largest in 3 months.
- EU corn yield estimate lowered ~5% to 6.61 mt/ha; Brazil 2025/26 second crop 92% harvested, 1st crop planting for 26/27 underway.
- Seasonal note: December corn has not peaked in October since 1980.

Soybeans
- Beans higher by ~0.12–0.14; meal steady to +$1; bean oil +40–50 points.
- First resistance for Nov-26 around $12.44½, then $12.56½ (weekly highs).
- Soybean oil weakness attributed to EPA SRE relief expectations for RINs (up to $1.8b). D4 RINs recent lows ~ $1.92.
- Crush margins near 5-month low; USDA flash soybean sale of 132k mt supports demand optimism.
- Crop ratings down 1% to 60% G/E; composite ratings weakest of the cycle; pods setting at 91%.

Wheat (CGO/KC)
- Prices spike to daily limit, CGO Dec-26 potentially trading above limit; new contract highs for CGO and KC.
- Technicals indicate strong upside risk: next resistance around CGO $7.77¼, KC $8.58.
- Global logistics: Russia’s Novorossiysk port repairs (1–4 months) and port access bottlenecks impacting grain exports; Danube/Sulina Canal vessel delays.
- Ukraine winter wheat plantings at risk due to drought; Russia hints at export measures; Egypt and other buyers boosting imports; EU soft wheat exports down ~33% YoY; Sudan buys French wheat.

Overall outlook
- Bullish near-term momentum in corn and wheat; soybeans supported by a new soybean sale and residual demand optimism.
- Watch for ongoing supply-side developments (US crop ratings, Brazil/Ukraine/Russia logistics, EPA RIN policy) as primary drivers in the near term.
- Key levels to monitor: Corn futures above $5 (Sept), Dec-26 highs; Soybeans resistance near $12.44–$12.56; CGO/KC targets near $7.77¼ and $8.58.

news.title: Crops Analysis | Grains score big at midweek - Pro Farmer
news.summary:
Summary: Agricultural commodities market outlook

- Corn: Bullish near-term with strong technical advantage; futures above $5.30 (Dec 2027) and trend suggests higher prices ahead. Advises cash-marketers to sell ~10% of 2027-28 production; 70% of 2026 crop forward-sold for cash-markets, and 60% hedged for hedgers.
- Soybeans: Fresh multi-year highs, with Nov 2027 futures well above $12.00. Recommend cash-marketers start sales of ~10% of 2027 production; ~75% of 2026 production sold/hedged at 65% covered for hedgers.
- Wheat: Prices boosted by geopolitical news (Putin about dead-end peace talks; Black Sea disruptions). Watch USDA export sales report (expected 200,000–550,000 MT). Technicals show resistance around $7.60 and support near $7.28; near-term upside risk remains.
- Cotton: Receives some supportive spillover from grain rally; December cotton remains in an uptrend with key resistance near 92.50 cents and support near 85.00 cents; current direction appears bullish but stock-specific factors will matter.

Overall: The market is broadly bullish across corn and soybeans, with price signals driven by supply disruptions and geopolitical developments. Traders should consider managed exposure via partial sales and hedges as outlined, while monitoring ongoing reports (USDA export sales, weather, and Black Sea supply dynamics) for directional shifts.

news.title: Citi Elevates Grain Targets as Super El Nino Risk Rises
news.summary:
Citi’s agricultural outlook argues for a bullish tilt in grains and select soft commodities into late 2026/early 2027, driven by a stronger-than-expected Super El Niño and multiple catalysts. Key points:

- El Niño risk: NOAA data shows >90% probability of a very strong El Niño and a 69% chance it surpasses all since 1950 in Oct–Dec, underpinning the adverse weather scenario Citi foresees for global crops.
- Price targets raised: Citi lifts 3-month and 12-month targets for corn, soybeans, and wheat:
  - Corn: 3m $5.40/bu; 12m $5.90/bu
  - Soybeans: 3m $12.75/bu; 12m $13.25/bu
  - Wheat: 3m $7.25/bu; 12m $7.75/bu
- Production-at-Risk framework: Prices may understate downside risk to global production; Citi’s framework suggests more potential upside for prices from weather, El Niño, and supply disruptions.
- Commodities most exposed to weather risk: Palm oil, robusta coffee, rice, sugar, cocoa, and Australian wheat are highlighted as highly vulnerable, with regional concentration in Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and parts of Brazil.
- Weather/geopolitics as drivers: A confluence of weaker yields, strong export demand, Black Sea disruptions, fertilizer/energy costs, and biofuel demand supports a bullish thesis for agriculture.
- Wheat sensitivity: Wheat is identified as the most sensitive grain to the combined weather and geopolitical risks, with recent European heat/drought cutting production estimates.

Bottom line: Citi expects higher upside for key grains and several tropical/soft commodities due to an escalating El Niño-driven weather risk and correlated supply concerns, with the strongest implications for corn, soybeans, wheat, palm oil, and robutas coffee, especially in the affected regions.

news.title: Global corn market surges, driven by US, Europe crop concerns | Farm Online | ACT
news.summary:
Global corn leads the recent agricultural commodities rally as weather and crop conditions raise supply concerns in key regions.

Key points:
- Corn (Chicago futures) up ~4% for the week and ~5% for the month, driven by deteriorating US crop conditions: USDA ratings at 57% good-to-excellent, and Pro Farmer tour yield at 10.9 t/ha vs USDA 11.3 t/ha anticipated.
- Market questions whether US production forecasts are overly optimistic amid tighter supply.
- Europe faces worsening maize outlook due to heat and drought; EU crop monitors cut maize yield to 6.61 t/ha, ~7% below the five-year average; EU soybean and sunflower yields also below average.
- Monsoon in India weak, reinforcing global supply concerns; wheat remains supported but less volatile amid Black Sea export disruption and ample Russian supply.
- Overall market dynamic: corn emerges as the lead grain due to weather-driven risk, with wheat activity more restrained; Black Sea disruptions persist but do not create a full-scale shortage signal yet.
- Australia-specific context: regional variability in crop prospects (South Australia strong; parts of WA vulnerable); local prices down in several ports; input costs easing slightly but fertilizer remains below year-ago levels.
- Outlook drivers to watch: September rainfall impacts on soybeans, corn, and pulses; soil moisture and spring rainfall influencing late-season wheat and rapeseed planting.

Implications for outlook:
- The global corn complex is the primary driver of near-term price action due to US and European weather risk.
- Wheat remains supported but less volatile; regional disruptions and shipping flows continue to shape prices.
- Fertilizer costs easing modestly provides some input-cost relief, but macro weather risk remains the dominant factor for crop markets.

news.title: A Speculation On Why Global Food Markets Are Rallying | RealClearMarkets
news.summary:
Summary:

The article argues that global food markets are rallying not because physical scarcity is imminent, but due to psychology and policy-driven supply anticipation. Key points:

- Global food inflation could rise from ~2.8% (H1 2026) to ~5% (H1 2027) as vulnerabilities in supply chains (notably fertilizer) surface. A major risk is the Gulf fertiliser chokepoint (half of world urea supply) and possible prolonged disruption.
- El Niño (likely to intensify) could push acutely food-insecure people from 225 million to about 274 million, with sharp regional impacts (Central America, Southern Africa). This supports elevated risk premiums.
- Market mechanics: bullish sentiment can pull futures up before physical scarcity materializes. Governments preemptively stockpile and restrict exports (e.g., China on phosphate, Russia on urea/DAP) while others sign bilateral deals, creating a divergence between perceived scarcity and actual on-hand inventories.
- FAO data suggests 2026 cereal production remains high (2.983 billion tonnes; only ~1.9% below 2025) with stock-to-use near 32%, indicating tight pockets rather than a global shortage. Wheat declines exist due to drought; maize is stronger in other regions.
- National responses indicate hedging against volatility: price supports and reserves (China), ongoing output expansion (Brazil), European Fertiliser Action Plan, and bilateral supply pacts (Philippines, Singapore) to improve resilience.
- The near-term price moves are driven by sentiment and hedging gaps between reported inventory and perceived scarcity, rather than immediate stockouts. The market is currently leaning on sentiment more than physical inventories, though reserve-building quietly narrows the gap.

Bottom line for agricultural commodities market outlook:
- Expect continued volatility driven by supply-chain bottlenecks, fertilizer constraints, and El Niño risks.
- Bulls may persist as traders price in potential shortages, even if current stocks appear adequate in many regions.
- Policy actions and bilateral supply agreements could mitigate some risk but may also tighten liquidity in global markets. The divergence between sentiment-driven futures and actual on-hand inventories remains a key watch item.

**근거:**

   현재 종가(28.02)가 트레일링 스탑(28.03) 아래로 내려왔습니다(청산 시그널: True). 추세추종 시스템에서 ‘보유 중인 포지션의 종가가 트레일링 스탑을 하향 돌파하면 즉시 청산한다’는 규칙은 어떤 예측이나 보조지표보다 우선합니다. 20일·100일 상단 돌파 신호도 모두 False이므로 신규 진입 근거는 없으며, 기존 롱 포지션을 정리하는 것이 유일한 기계적 대응입니다.

2. **뉴스 팩트가 ‘추세 피로/저항 구간’을 뒷받침**  
   - **BBH 코멘터리(FXStreet)**: DXY가 200일 이동평균선(≈99.17) 근처에서 저항을 맞고 횡보 중이며, 인플레이션은 둔화세인데 실질 소비가 약해져 연준이 공격적 긴축 대신 ‘홀드’로 갈 여지가 크다고 분석합니다. 시장은 9월 인상 확률을 36% 정도로만 반영 중이라 “비둘기파적 재평가(dovish repricing)” 시 달러 약세 압력이 열려 있다고 봅니다.  
   - **ING(Jackson Hole 프리뷰)**: 핵심 PCE가 0.2% MoM/3.3% YoY로 디스인플레이션 추세 확인, 실질 소비 정체 → 9월 금리 동결 전망이 우세하지만, 워시 연설이 매파적으로 읽히면 DXY가 99.0 근처에서 일시 반등할 수 있다고 봅니다. “근본적 편향은 약달러이나 단기 변동성 확대”가 핵심입니다.  
   - **Convera/Kevin Ford & TMGM**: DXY가 99.00~99.75(200일 EMA) 박스권에 갇혀 있으며, 200일 EMA 상향 돌파 전까지는 약세 편향 유지. 워시 연설·고용·CPI 전까지 방향성 부재.  

   이들 기사는 공통으로 **“현재 레벨(99 전후)이 강한 저항대이며, 펀더멘털 모멘텀이 약해 추가 상승 동력이 부족하다”**는 팩트를 전합니다. 기계적 트레일링 스탑이 맞춰진 최근 고점(≈28.12 수준)에서 3×ATR(0.27) 만큼 후퇴한 28.03이 정확히 이 저항대 상단과 맞물려 있어, 시스템이 ‘추세 연장 실패’를 감지하고 청산한 것으로 해석됩니다.

3. **일목균형표(보조 참고)는 양운·구름 안 → ‘급락 아닌 조정’ 시사**  
   현재 구름 안(양운)이므로 추세 붕괴보다는 건강한 조정 국면일 확률이 높습니다. 다만 규칙상 청산 신호가 났으므로 **전량 청산 후 재진입(상단 돌파 시) 대기**가 정석입니다. 양운이 유지된다면 추후 20일/100일 상단 돌파 시 재진입 비중을 평소대로 가져가면 됩니다.

**결론:** 규칙대로 **기존 보유 물량 전량 매도(청산)** 실행. 뉴스는 ‘저항대에서 모멘텀 소진’을 확인시켜 주는 팩트일 뿐, 매도 결정을 바꾼 것이 아님. 재진입은 종가가 20일/100일 상단을 돌파할 때 기계적으로 진입.

news.title: US Dollar: Fed repricing risk weighs on usd – BBH
news.summary:
BBH commentary on the US dollar outlook:

- The USD remains consolidating after recent gains, with the DXY testing its 200-day moving average around 99.17.
- Core drivers: PCE inflation is above the Fed’s 2% target while real consumer spending is weakening, giving the Fed room to hold rates instead of tightening aggressively.
- Fed pricing: Markets still price only modest tightening ahead (around 40 basis points total over the next year; roughly 36% odds of a 25bp hike at the Sept meeting).
- Peso on the Fed: The stance described as dovish for the dollar—fewer near-term rate hikes could weaken the USD as expectations shift.
- Broader context: The Jackson Hole gathering starts, with potential limited forward guidance from Fed Chair Warsh; markets will watch for communications framework, balance sheet, and inflation strategies from the Fed’s task forces.
- Commodity and tech note: Brent under $90, Nvidia earnings reinforce AI-driven capex backdrop, contributing to risk-on sentiment that can support a softer dollar if USD repricing begins.

In short, BBH sees the dollar as vulnerable to a dovish repricing given sticky but non-accelerating inflation and softening real spending, with markets unlikely to price in aggressive Fed tightening in the near term. The DXY faces resistance near the 200-day moving average, but the outcome hinges on Fed messaging post-Jackson Hole.

news.title: US Dollar: Warsh speech keeps markets cautious – ING
news.summary:
Summary: The ING view ahead of Jackson Hole remains cautiously bearish for the US dollar, though risks tilt the other way on hawkish shifts. Key takeaways:
- PCE data show disinflation intact but still gradual. Core PCE at 0.2% MoM / 3.3% YoY; headline PCE at 0.2% MoM / 3.7% YoY. Inflation trends support a hold but keep rate hikes on the table less likely.
- The Fed is expected to hold rates on 16 September. ING expects a weaker dollar on a balance of data and Fed guidance, but acknowledges hawkish pricing around Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech could lift DXY toward 99.0.
- Data mix: July real spending flat as households save more; real disposable income flatlining for over a year. This soft growth backdrop favors a hold path, though markets price ~50% odds of a hike by decision day, which could rise with further hawkish signals.
- Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech is a potential catalyst. If markets read his remarks as hawkish, dollar upside could re-emerge despite a general hold scenario.
- FX implications: EUR/USD hovering around 1.1650 amid uncertain USD direction; risk sentiment and Nvidia-like upside can provide some USD support, but the broader bias remains toward a weaker dollar if the Fed stays on hold and data keep disinflation on track.
- Near-term focus: Jackson Hole remarks and the upcoming NFP revision; markets may not want to push USD shorts aggressively ahead of Warsh, keeping DXY supported around 99.0 ahead of the event.

Bottom line for DXY: The macro setup leans toward a hold in September and a softer dollar, but Jackson Hole and any hawkish Fedspeak could briefly prop up the dollar and push DXY toward 99.0. The longer-term bias remains a weaker dollar if the data keep inflation slowly trending down and the Fed maintains a cautious stance.

news.title: US data keeps Fed hawks in play | Convera
news.summary:
Summary: The US dollar's near-term direction remains unclear, as mixed inflation data and geopolitics keep Fed hawks engaged but not decisively moving the dollar. Key points for the DXY:

- Inflation data: July PCE rose modestly (headline +0.2%, +3.7% y/y; core PCE in line). Services inflation firm. This supports a cautious, hawkish Fed stance but not a clear trigger for a rally.
- Growth and demand: GDP at 1.5% with solid durable goods (driven by transport) and wage-income dynamics improving household savings. The data has not shifted the probability of a September hike meaningfully (markets price roughly a 42% chance).
- Yield/curves: Two-year yield rose on firm inflation, but long end contained by Treasury buybacks, steepening the curve and weakening the traditional yield-dollar link.
- Warsh influence: A hawkish or vague Jackson Hole signal from Kevin Warsh could lift the DXY toward 99.50–100.00; ambiguity could leave payrolls/CPI as the main drivers.
- Geopolitical and fiscal risk: Hormuz-related developments and US fiscal credibility concerns add downside pressure on the dollar; gold’s strength (~14% monthly) signals risk hedging rather than pure policy expectations.
- USD/CAD dynamics: USD/CAD sits in a 1.3760–1.3900 range, with 1.3900 as key resistance. A break above 1.3900 could push toward 1.4000–1.4100; a break below 1.3760 could target 1.3500–1.3700. Canadian data (Q2 GDP) and US policy signals will shape the pair.
- Near-term guidance: Rates are currently the clearest near-term indicator for USD direction. A credible hawkish Warsh message could support the dollar; in the absence of clarity, payrolls and CPI will be decisive for September expectations.

Bottom line: The DXY is consolidating near 99.00 with limited momentum. The next move hinges on Warsh’s Jackson Hole guidance and upcoming payrolls/CPI data, with risk skewed by geopolitics and fiscal concerns. In the immediate term, a test of 98.80 support or a push toward 99.50–100.00 remains contingent on new inflation signals and policy cues.

news.title: The Dollar Index is climbing out of a fiscal hole
news.summary: Summary: US Dollar Index (DXY) is trading a touch above 99.00, with near-term resistance around the 200-day EMA near 99.75 and support near 98.50–99.00. The recent move higher followed a Treasury buyback expansion rather than a Fed shift, pulling DXY off its three-month low. Markets assign roughly 40% odds to a Sept rate hike (vs. ~60% for hold) with Dec still pricing a single 25 bp move later in the year; October pricing implies a higher probability of tightening, but the overall rate story remains tentative. Technicals show the 200-day EMA as a key cap; a close above 99.75 would re-open the 100.00/101.75 area, while a break below 98.50 could invite further downside. Bias remains bearish while 99.75 caps; invalidation requires a daily close above 99.75. The core driver remains monetary policy expectations, with the Fed’s inflation/ employment dynamics shaping the dollar’s trajectory.

news.title: United States Dollar Index gains support as strong US data sparks rate hike expectations
news.summary:
US Dollar Index (DXY) outlook – macro analysis

- Current view: DXY remains bid but with a cautious, fragile recovery. Trading around 99.20, technically capped below the 50-period EMA and holding just above the 9-period EMA, suggesting modest upside pressure but no decisive breakout.

- Key driver: Strong US data, notably July PCE inflation at 0.2% m/m (vs 0.1% expected) and core inflation still firm, reinforcing expectations for a potential final Fed rate hike this year. Markets look ahead to Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech for further guidance.

- Technical stance: Neutral-to-bearish near-term bias. RSI ~39.9 indicates limited upside momentum. Immediate support around 99.19 (9-EMA). Resistance sits near 99.91 (50-EMA); a daily close above this level could open a broader rebound, but the failure to clear it keeps the move constrained.

- Outlook considerations:
  - Hawkish US data keeps expectations of a late-year Fed hike alive, supporting the USD.
  - Warsh’s Jackson Hole remarks are a focal point; risk of increased volatility around the event could cap USD shorts.
  - Broad market backdrop (risk sentiment, oil/fiscal dynamics, and geopolitics) can influence DXY near-term, but the macro driver remains US inflation and Fed policy expectations.

Bottom line: The DXY is supported by firmer US inflation data and rate-hike expectations, yet faces technical resistance and a cautious stance ahead of Jackson Hole. Expect a stay range-bound near 99 with the next breakout dependent on stronger/clearer Fed cues.
